Q: Copy all files with a certain extension from all subdirectories A:

Use:

find [SOURCEPATH] -type f -name '[PATTERN]' | 
    while read P; do cp --parents "$P" [DEST]; done

You may remove the --parents option, but there is a risk of collision if multiple files bear the same name.

Q: Should I namespace global functions in PHP? A:

Just got a similar suggestion in VS Code and looked it up. Apparently there are certain functions that are pre-optimized by the compiler if it can unambiguously identify them without a namespace lookup.

There are about 36 special functions recognized by the PHP compiler, including strlen() and count(), that PHP can run significantly faster. The thing is, if you use them in a namespace (e.g., FOO), the compiler cannot be sure whether you mean \strlen() or \FOO\strlen(). Thus, the function call is not optimized.

Example:

<?php
namespace FOO;
use function count;

strlen($text);     // not optimized, ambiguous name
\strlen($text);    // optimized
count([]);         // optimized

Source: https://blog.devsense.com/2025/optimize-native-function-invocation/

This is almost certainly a micro-optimization that most programs don't need to worry about. If one were to want to do this anyway, here is the list of functions currently being optimized (in a table so it's not super long.)
array_key_exists array_slice boolval call_user_func call_user_func_array
chr clone count defined doubleval
floatval func_get_args func_num_args get_called_class get_class
gettype in_array intval is_array is_bool
is_double is_float is_int is_integer is_long
is_null is_object is_resource is_scalar is_string
ord sizeof sprintf strlen strval

Source: https://github.com/php/php-src/blob/PHP-8.5/Zend/zend_compile.c#L4978

Q: Move files to directories based on extension A:

You can use a for loop to traverse through folders and subfolders inside the source folder.

The following code will help you move files in pair from "/source/foler/path/" to "/destination/fodler/path/". This code will move files matching their name and having different extensions.

for d in /source/folder/path/*; do
    ls -tr $d |grep txt | rev | cut -f 2 -d '.' | rev | uniq | head -n 4 | xargs -I % bash -c 'mv -v '$d'/%.{txt,csv} /destination/folder/path/'
    sleep 30
done

Q: Button Packing in Wrong Spot A:

Not sure why the label's parent is root. If the button needs to be below the label, then the label's parent should be the room_container. root has no idea what room_container is doing.

room_container = tk.Frame(main_container)
room_container.grid(row=0, column=0, sticky="nsew")
# Without this, the button will be stuck
# to the bottom of the label
room_container.grid_rowconfigure(1, weight=1)
room_container.grid_columnconfigure(0, weight=1)
room_container.configure(background="green")

# Parent has been changed to room_container
label = tk.Label(room_container,text="You make your way towards the cave entrance... \nbut who are you anyways?",
                   fg = "black",
                   bg = "grey",
                   font=("Papyrus",30)
                   )
label.grid(row=0,column=0,columnspan=10,sticky=tk.N)

# This button will appear in the centre between 
# the label and the next frame
room_selected = Battle(room_container)
room_selected.grid(row=1, column=0)

Q: adding a float dictionary value to a variable that is a float A:

descriptive name

dict = {

Ok, that's just a terrible name, as there is already a builtin named dict(). Please avoid shadowing builtin names in that way. Maybe menu, or food_to_price, would be a better approach to naming.

    for char in itemlist:

Here, char should be named item or food, since we're dealing with multi-character strings.

        items = input("Items pls").lower().title()

That's the wrong name, as it is plural. You meant item. OTOH itemlist might plausibly be named items.

Also, calling .lower() has no useful effect, as we immediately override with .title()

re-initializing within the loop

        itemlist = [""]
        itemlist.append(items)

That doesn't make sense. It's equivalent to itemlist = ["", items]

            price = 0
            price += dict[char]

Similarly, that is simply assigning price = dict[char].

Prefer to initialize before executing the loop body. Also, I suspect you want empty list [] rather than [""], which contains a single element that doesn't appear on the menu.

Q: What's the purpose of the socket option SO_SNDLOWAT A:

FYI: Linux does not implement this for a reason: while it seems it makes life easier in userland, the effort saved in userland is greater than the effort spent in the kernel.

99.9% of the time, if you care, you should not hit this, if you do fix your app with configuration settings. The ocde to deal with partials is inevitable.

Implementing this has been rejected by Linux kernel devs, seemingly for good reasons.

Q: Why are IntelliJ inspections suddenly not running in my editor? A:

Found the problem.

The content root within my project (~/Documents/Sites/xenforo) is a symbolic link, and it looks like when I originally marked it as my content root, IntelliJ decided to instead add the destination folder of the symbolic link to my project rather than marking the symbolic link as the content root, so when I opened files through my symbolic link, it was not considered part of the source files despite being the same files as present within the symbolic link's target folder which IntelliJ had added to the project.

I can't seem to get IntelliJ to recognize my symbolic link as the content root, it just keeps adding the target folder to the project instead. I'll probably just ignore the primary project folder from now on and open files through the symlink's target folder.
